claim: For \(X_n=(S^0)^{\circledast(n+1)}\), the unique \(2n+2\)-point minimal finite model of \(S^n\) for \(n\ge 1\), every continuous map \(f:X_n\to X_m\) induces a null-homotopic map \(|K(f)|:S^n\to S^m\) unless \(n=m\) and \(f\) is a homeomorphism. Hence minimal sphere models directly realize only the zero class when \(n\ne m\), and exactly the degree classes \(-1,0,1\) when \(n=m\); in particular no nonzero unstable class with \(n>m\), and no self-map of degree \(|d|\ge 2\), is represented without enlarging or subdividing the finite model.

integrity.claim_scope: homotopy classes of sphere maps induced directly by continuous maps between canonical minimal finite sphere models
integrity.novelty_boundary: the 2026 facet-essential Whitehead theorem overlaps only the equal-dimensional weak-equivalence endpoint; the cross-dimensional all-n,m rigidity is the substantive extension checked here
integrity.proof_core: strict target-rank growth for noncollapsed source levels plus the cone image forced by a collapsed level

scientific_limitations: No lower bound is proved for the size of an enlarged or subdivided finite model needed to represent a prescribed nontrivial sphere map.
Two older highly relevant construction papers could not be inspected in full because publisher access required human verification; accessible abstracts were checked and are specific constructions.
Literature and database noncoverage searches reduce but do not eliminate the possibility of an equivalent result stated under different terminology.
title: Map rigidity of minimal finite sphere models
